executiveSummary: GM1911's 2025 identity, centre, population, 67 neighbourhoods, 19 districts, 19 BAG places, 50 settlement labels, Anna Paulowna station and nine logical road corridors are broadly coherent. Three BAG label points remain outside both the generated and independently retrieved full CBS boundary and must be retained as a version/label-point caveat rather than rejected. The complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes, but release is correction-required. At T+24 the generic coastal preset produces 2.272482 m direct depth, 31,554 affected resident-equivalents and 557,710.056 deprived person-hours without selecting a Wadden Sea or IJsselmeer level, primary-defence state, breach/overtopping location, polder compartment, arrival, duration or dewatering curve. Official evidence instead distinguishes the Wieringermeer around six metres below NAP, Leemans/Lely pumping, local primary and regional defences, the Afsluitdijk and Den Oever discharge complex, freshwater supply and salinity. Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire reuse the same neighbourhood ranking despite different mechanisms. A road-only generic service graph cannot represent the A7 Afsluitdijk gateway, Anna Paulowna rail, dispersed villages, acute-care access, water-control chain, provider systems or Agriport's agri-energy-data activity. Public observations, forecasts, registers and plans constrain exercises but establish neither live asset state nor T+72 restoration. Unknown and NoData must never be rendered as zero or safe, and exact local consequences remain synthetic until a source-valid scenario and action ledger are selected.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1911 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS feature retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1911 as Hollands Kroon in Noord-Holland and reports 49,982 residents, density 140/km², 22.6% aged 65 or older and 7,848 one-person households; the generated centre [4.936634497718845,52.82567386500721] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Sixty-seven neighbourhood rows in nineteen districts sum to 49,980 residents, two below the municipality total (-0.004%); households sum to 22,450 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 11,290. Allocation reconciles to 49,982 without rewriting source observations.

BAG supplies nineteen active woonplaatsen and BRT supplies fifty labels—27 woonkernen, thirteen buurtschappen, seven gehuchten and three deelkernen. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0; labels are not occupancy, catchment, defence or service footprints.

The generated overview MultiPolygon has 245 coordinate positions versus 10,547 in the fresh non-generalized feature. BAG label points for Zijdewind, Den Oever and Wieringerwerf fall outside both versions; the result is retained as a cross-edition label-point/polygon caveat and is not evidence that these official places are outside the municipality. Cars-per-household covers 59/67 neighbourhoods, while district heat and charging cover 0/67; missing and suppressed values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Adopted Omgevingsvisie Hollands Kroon 2040 and local water, access and activity pathways
supports: The adopted vision distinguishes Wieringermeer, Noordelijk Westfriesland, Wieringen and Anna Paulowna/Wieringerwaardpolder. It states that Wieringermeer lies about six metres below NAP and that pumping stations Leemans and Lely are essential for water management; this is planning/mechanism evidence, not live pump or defence state.

Fresh water arrives from the IJsselmeer and supports drinking water, nature and agriculture. The vision describes growing salinity through seepage and seawater, sensitive bulb growing in Anna Paulownapolder and along the IJsselmeer coast, tighter freshwater availability and explicit prioritisation of vital drinking-water and safety functions.

The A7 is the main north-south connection for Wieringermeer and Agriport. The document identifies Wieringerwerf as regional centre, Anna Paulowna as a station/service centre, a need for better public transport particularly in the east, and locally organised care in a dispersed rural municipality.

Agriport is an above-regional agri-energy-data and greenhouse cluster; CBS separately records 640 residents, 100 businesses and 295 non-residential buildings in Bedrijventerrein Agriport. The public PDF has an adopted date and municipality-wide policy coverage but no raw operational API, fixed refresh cadence or standard redistribution licence; it cannot supply incident occupancy, load, stock, failure or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Adopted Policy Plan 2024–2027, current published risk profile and 72-hour resilience context
evidenceSources.edition: Policy plan adopted 15 March 2024; organisation page still publishes Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2022–2024; pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted plan prioritises preparation for extreme weather including flooding and for electricity failure. Its regional risk material also identifies overstroming, loss of vital services, extreme weather, care-continuity disruption, gas-pipeline incident, water incident and nature fire.

The current authority page still links the 2022–2024 risk profile while the plan envisaged a new method/profile in 2025. That publication state must be versioned; it cannot silently be described as a current local probability or incident forecast.

VRNHN's December 2025 emergency-support-point pilot explicitly examines help for less self-reliant people during prolonged power or drinking-water outage and how residents can remain self-reliant for 72 hours. This supports action design, not a promise that a point, resource or service is available in Hollands Kroon.

These are adopted/public documentary sources with regional coverage and dated editions but no machine event cadence or standard redistribution licence identified. Facility readiness, staffing, communications, resources, mutual aid and decision status remain Unknown until exercise-specific evidence is supplied.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Hollands Kroon water-system works, Wieringermeerkering and Den Oever–Den Helder primary-defence evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current public project hub and project pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: HHNK reports that Kolhorn-Westfriesedijk and Kolhorn De Strook lack required height, several Schagerkogge boezem defences require improvement, and parts of the Den Oever–Den Helder primary line do not meet the latest standards. A project statement is not a breach, current instability or probability.

The Wieringermeerkering protects areas around Amstelmeer and Wieringermeer. HHNK states that Westerlanderdijk, Amsteldiepdijk, Ulkesluis and Haukeskeersluis need no reinforcement under the cited assessment, while Haukesschutsluis does not meet the water-safety norm and is at end of life; future variants are still being evaluated.

The Den Oever–Den Helder project distinguishes Wieringer Zeewering, Amsteldiepdijk and Balgzanddijk and identifies revetment/internal-stability deficiencies in bounded sections. Wieringermeer inlet projects increase future inflow capacity, and HHNK describes Leemans as the polder's most important pump.

The webpages provide named local asset/project and assessment context with publication/project status but no standard machine cadence or standard reuse licence found. They do not establish event-valid gate position, pump availability, connected catchment, residual capacity, breach, inundation footprint or dewatering time.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO 2025 flood-candidate and Waterinfo Wadden Sea/IJsselmeer point context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; Waterinfo snapshot retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO is professional flood-preparedness information requiring specialist water-manager interpretation. Exact containment against the full 2025 municipality boundary finds six primary-defence candidate points—two Balgzanddijk, two Wieringermeerdijk and two Wieringerzeewering—and 297 regional candidates. They are catalogue candidates, not selected breach locations or inundation footprints.

The candidate query returns zero regional-system and zero outer-dike records in the separately named categories. Empty categories are no matching records in that layer/query, never zero regional-water or outer-dike risk; source edition, scenario, defence state, datum, cell, NoData and licence must accompany any selected raster.

The deployed Waterinfo snapshot has point observations at Den Oever IJsselmeer inner harbour (-25 cm NAP) and Wadden Sea outer harbour (-62 cm NAP) at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026. Forecast points exist through requested T+48, while the national public retrieval has no T+72 water-level forecast.

Waterinfo is generally CC0, commonly ten-minute observations and public non-mission-critical point service; its frontend forecast endpoint is not a stable external contract. LIWO is release-versioned and layer-specific terms must be resolved. Point levels are not municipal inundation, defence condition or a calendar-unbound scenario, and missing T+72 is NoData rather than zero.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Afsluitdijk, NWB roads, rail station, scheduled transit and observed road-situation context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS/NDW deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026; RWS project page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Rijkswaterstaat identifies the 32 km Afsluitdijk as water defence, freshwater, road/water-transport and economic infrastructure. The Stevin complex at Den Oever and Lorentz complex at Kornwerderzand discharge IJsselmeer surplus to the Wadden Sea; the A7 links Noord-Holland and Fryslân and carries thousands of vehicles daily.

The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph exposes nine named Hollands Kroon route records over A7, N99, N239, N240, N248, N242, N241 and N249 toward six municipalities. Nominal 150/260 values are scenario units, not measured lanes, throughput or emergency capacity.

The CC0 ProRail register locates one station, Anna Paulowna, and generated GTFS includes 77 stop areas. Static geometry and best-effort schedules do not establish current service, vehicle/passenger capacity, accessible evacuation, rail replacement or T+72 recovery.

The nearest timestamped NDW situation in the deployment snapshot is about 9.79 km from the municipality reference point. A proximity/no-match query does not prove any A7, Afsluitdijk, N-road, rail, bridge or local road is open. A dated November 2025 A7 closure showed a directional detour adding up to 90 minutes, useful as a validation case only, not a current closure.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water-asset, provider-responsibility and electricity-planning context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; provider feature timestamps 7 September 2025–24 March 2026
supports: The partial HWH IMWA/DAMO spatial assignment contains 1,166 GM1911 objects: 980 weirs, 149 surface-water pumps, 21 sewer pumps, fourteen sluices and two RWZIs named Wieringen and Wieringermeer. These are register points with contributor-dependent completeness, not connected topology, live state, available capacity or backup.

HWH Kunstwerken is national, weekly and CC BY-SA 4.0; Waterketen DAMO is national CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor timestamps and variable completeness. Object count or register absence cannot establish operating capacity, flow or safety.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS/WFS at the municipality reference point identifies Liander electricity (updated 24 March 2026), Liander gas (17 December 2025), PWN drinking water and Ziggo media (both 7 September 2025), and no drainage polygon. Territory is responsibility context, not cables, pipes, backhaul, coverage quality, outage or restoration; empty drainage is Unknown.

A single NBNL planning query for postcode 1774BK reports Liander station OS ULKESLUIS 10-1i, 20/17 MW existing/required withdrawal, 5.4 MW queued across 23 requests, 40/28 MW injection and 23 MW queued across fifteen requests, plus 33 projects with earliest 2026. At-least-quarterly/monthly planning data with no exact standard licence identified is neither municipality-wide coverage nor present load, spare capacity, outage or operator commitment.

evidenceSources.publisher: RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / IPO Risicokaart
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public communications, education, care, weather, air, seismic and nature-fire context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; Risicokaart metadata updated 19 February 2026
supports: RDI assigns 137 antenna installations—56 mobile, 33 fixed-link, 41 amateur, three broadcast and four other-mobile—and daily attribution-licensed DUO data assigns 28 education locations: 22 primary, one secondary and five other registered. These are registers, not coverage, occupancy, resilience, backup or dispatch capacity; RDI's standard licence/cadence is not stated.

The RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 questionnaire has no point in GM1911. From the municipal reference point, Noordwest Ziekenhuisgroep Den Helder and Dijklander Hoorn lie about 19.55 km and 21.37 km straight-line and report 24/7 emergency departments; questionnaire rooms/visits are dated context, not travel time, staffing, admission capacity or guaranteed access.

The nearest KNMI station is De Kooy Airport about 15.35 km from the reference point in the retrieved 10-minute CC BY 4.0 snapshot. One indicative RIVM air point, Wieringerwerf-Medemblikkerweg, is inside the municipality; a single timestamped value is not area exposure or forecast. The nearest retrieved seismic origin is an induced M1.72 event around Noordbeemster, 28.13 km from the reference point, dated 21 July 2026; an origin is not local motion, damage or probability.

The Public Domain Risicokaart combustible-nature WFS returns no feature whose representative point is inside the generated GM1911 polygon, while the municipal vision names Robbenoordbos and Dijkgatsbos. That is a coverage/association gap rather than no fuel or safe nature area. Polygons prove eligibility only, never current ignition, moisture, smoke, perimeter or suppression.

Zijdewind, Den Oever and Wieringerwerf BAG label points fall outside both versions. Preserve the official places and compare full BAG place polygons/editions rather than snapping or excluding them.
Wadden Sea, IJsselmeer, Amstelmeer, Wieringermeer compartments, primary/regional defences, boezem, inlets, pumps, salinity and drainage cannot be inferred from municipality or neighbourhood centres.

notes: Official/generated population is 49,982, density 140/km², age 65+ is 22.6% and one-person households number 7,848.

Registered residents do not include incident-time workers, pupils, care users, tourists, mariners, contractors, responders or displaced people, especially at Agriport, Den Oever, stations, ports and large rural sites.

regionalDetail.summary: Neighbourhood detail is strong, but sparse statistics and infrastructure registers retain source-specific coverage limits.

Provider areas, antenna and school registers, care questionnaire, air point and weather station remain descriptive official context with affectsSimulation=false.

The three outlying BAG centres remain official reference points; label containment alone does not determine place membership, population or service allocation.
Settlement labels are not evacuation zones, catchments, occupancy, self-reliance, care access or hazard footprints.

transport.summary: Reference roads, rail and transit exist, but the causal graph is road-only and misses gateway, modal and local-access failure states.
notes: Nine logical NWB records connect six neighbours by A7 and seven N-roads; one ProRail station and 77 GTFS stop areas provide reference geometry/schedules.

The A7 over the Afsluitdijk is simultaneously a long-distance gateway and part of a water-control structure, but the graph has no structure/gate, direction, closure, detour, rail-transfer or local access state.
All nominal road capacities are scenario units. NDW proximity/no-match and GTFS schedules never prove passability, service, capacity or restoration through T+72.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong local risk, water, infrastructure and 72-hour preparedness evidence exists, but no public source establishes a selected live incident or response state.
notes: Official evidence supports extreme weather, flooding, electricity loss, care continuity, Wadden/IJsselmeer controls, polder pumping, salinity, dispersed access and nature-fire eligibility as distinct planning concerns.
Current public Waterinfo/KNMI/air/NDW records have source time and limited point/record coverage and cannot be projected onto a calendar-unbound simulation or through T+72.

Asset assessment, design capacity, provider territory, congestion planning, school/antenna/care registration and 72-hour pilot participation are context, not current availability or action commitment.
Unknown facility occupancy, utility topology, backup, staffing, stock, passability, pump/gate state and restoration must remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical scenarios execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1911 pnpm audit:model passed the two complete coverage tests for ten presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/facilities/supply.

Focused reproductions captured municipality, local-allocation, service and recovery values without adding a repository test file. River-flood remains exact zero at T+24 and T+72 because the canonical preset is narrowly scoped; that is not zero Wadden, IJsselmeer, canal, regional-water, groundwater or rainfall risk.
Wildfire T+24 has direct flame zero, smoke 0.211134 and zero current affected resident-equivalents; earthquake current motion is exact zero. These are preset states, not proof of no local hazard.
All outputs remain deterministic exercise indices/resident-equivalents, not observations, probabilities, casualties, measured inundation or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability remains in [0,1]; hazards, demand, delivery, affected residents and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exact zero event hazard, affected population and event-attributable burden; repeated runs are deterministic and burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 67 neighbourhoods and reconciles to 49,982 residents; local demand/delivery closes to municipality totals and changing the selected map layer does not change the scenario.
Passing arithmetic does not validate coastal hydraulics, polder drainage, spatial allocation, transient/activity exposure, service topology or restoration precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic coast screens and a common seed override defence, polder, rain, heat, infrastructure and fuel geography.
notes: Coastal T+24 reaches 2.272482 m direct depth and 31,554 affected without a selected Wadden/IJsselmeer level, defence/breach, hydraulic compartment, terrain-connected footprint, arrival, duration or recession.

Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire at T+24 share the exact leading order Winkel southeast of Dorpsstraat, Buitengebied Anna Paulowna, Middenmeer Centrum, Kreileroord and De Haukes; compound converges to the same order at T+72.

Official evidence instead distinguishes Wieringermeer depth/pumps, Anna Paulowna and IJsselmeer-coast salinity, Wadden/Amstelmeer/IJsselmeer defences, Agriport activity, named forest areas and road/rail gateways.
Administrative centres and a stable seed cannot stand in for flood cells, source distance, eligible fuel, imperviousness, heat/soil covariates, utility/service areas or exposed-object geometry.

serviceDependencies.summary: Generic road-derived service flows omit the physical water chain, sector-specific utilities, activity exposure, care referral and multimodal access.
notes: NWB proves road geometry only, yet the logical service graph uses generic cross-border route/capacity semantics for lifelines without evidence of feeders, pressure zones, pumps, telecom backhaul, facility catchments or stock chains.
The model has no typed Wadden/IJsselmeer–defence–sluice–polder–pump–drainage/freshwater relationship even though official evidence makes those dependencies central.

Agriport's 295 non-residential buildings and 100 businesses, Anna Paulowna station, Den Oever gateway/port, schools, antennas and external acute-care access cannot alter service demand, affected activity or downstream consequence.
Provider territories and one NBNL sample identify responsibility/planning context only; they cannot justify exact T+24 service availability or T+72 repair.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers reconcile, but local event selection, source class and accountable first-72-hour actions are outside the causal graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.

Waterinfo, LIWO candidates, HWH, Mijn Aansluiting, NBNL, RDI, DUO, RIVM, KNMI, Risicokaart and NDW correctly remain affectsSimulation=false; current records must not silently alter synthetic scenario time.

The trace does not identify a selected defence/hydraulic event, rainfall/polder model, salinity/freshwater allocation, wildfire target, cyber target, road/rail state, worker/visitor exposure or facility/utility operating state.
First-72-hour actions lack accountable owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification and rollback fields.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery is deterministic but unsupported by local dewatering, gateway, utility, care, supply or response evidence.
notes: Coastal direct forcing/depth is zero by T+72, but 9,936 resident-equivalents remain affected and cumulative burden reaches 1,755,947.233 person-hours; service availability ranges from supply 0.617901 to mobility 0.890172.
Compound T+72 retains depth/stress 0.566166, severity 0.538252, 30,300 affected and 1,928,121.126 person-hours; service availability ranges from telecom 0.247756 to mobility 0.841032.

No selected source establishes defence access, pump/gate operation, compartment dewatering, freshwater allocation, Afsluitdijk/N-road/rail passability, acute-care referral, utility switching, stocks, crews or repair milestones.
Expose results as synthetic exercise trajectories and avoid implying restoration promises until action and evidence-valid recovery curves are scenario-bound.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, municipality centre and resident controls reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM1911, Hollands Kroon, Noord-Holland and Noord-Holland-Noord agree; the centre is contained. CBS reports 49,982 residents and 67 neighbourhoods sum to 49,980 (-0.004%).
findings.action: Retain source editions, licence, suppression/null semantics and published-versus-allocated reconciliation without rewriting the two-person publication difference.

findings.summary: Unavailable statistics and empty public queries are preserved as Unknown rather than false zero or safe state.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging, drainage-provider territory, T+72 Waterinfo, in-boundary acute-care point and exact combustible-area matches are missing/empty in their specific sources; none establishes physical absence or safety.
findings.action: Keep coverage, query/effective time, edition, quality, suppression and NoData semantics through ingestion, simulation eligibility and UI; render scoped zero separately from Unknown.

findings.summary: Three official BAG label points fall outside both generated and fresh full CBS municipality polygons.
findings.evidence: Zijdewind, Den Oever and Wieringerwerf reproduce as outside the 245-position overview and 10,547-position full 2025 feature, while municipal/CBS identity evidence plainly retains these places.
findings.action: Retain the places and expose a BAG/CBS edition and label-point caveat. Compare full woonplaats polygons against full municipality geometry before changing membership; never snap points or infer exclusion from a label-point test.

findings.summary: A generic coast-distance function emits an unsupported exact 2.272482 m direct depth and first-72-hour burden.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reaches severity 0.748900, depth 2.272482 m, 31,554 affected and 557,710.056 person-hours; T+72 has zero current forcing/depth but 9,936 affected and 1,755,947.233 cumulative hours. No Wadden/IJsselmeer level, named defence/breach, compartment, arrival, duration or dewatering curve is selected.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing direct depth, exposure and recovery until an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/HHNK/RWS event intersects full geometry. Keep coast proximity diagnostic and Wadden, IJsselmeer, Amstelmeer, regional-water, polder seepage and pluvial mechanisms as separate Unknown states.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated active hazards reuse one neighbourhood ordering.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire T+24 all begin with Winkel southeast of Dorpsstraat, Buitengebied Anna Paulowna, Middenmeer Centrum, Kreileroord and De Haukes; compound converges to the same order by T+72 despite official hazard-specific geography.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces and exposed-object intersections. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking only after evidence-derived values and keep unsupported cells Unknown rather than pseudo-precise.

findings.summary: Deep-polder drainage, defence, pumping, freshwater and salinity dependencies are absent from the causal model.
findings.evidence: The adopted vision places Wieringermeer about six metres below NAP and calls Leemans/Lely essential; HHNK identifies named primary/regional defences, Haukesschutsluis and inlet works; HWH supplies 1,166 partial water objects. None governs model drainage, water, mobility or recovery.
findings.action: Add a typed water graph with distinct sea/lake boundary, primary/regional defence, compartment/boezem, sluice/inlet, pump/drainage, freshwater availability and salinity states. Bind design capacity only with event-valid operator state; otherwise use Unknown and a transparent synthetic fallback.

findings.summary: The Afsluitdijk/Den Oever complex is reduced to a generic road edge despite coupled water-control and gateway roles.
findings.evidence: RWS documents defence, IJsselmeer discharge, freshwater, navigation and A7 functions. The graph exposes a nominal A7 route to Súdwest-Fryslân but no named structure, direction, gate/sluice, closure, detour, water-operation interaction or verification state.
findings.action: Represent the A7 crossing as a mobility/supply-only typed gateway with direction, passability, alternative route and event-valid observation; keep sluice/pump/defence states in the water graph and couple them only through explicit documented rules.

findings.summary: Road-derived logical flows cannot substantiate electricity, water, drainage, gas, telecom, facilities or exact supply restoration.
findings.evidence: NWB provides roads and scenario-unit capacities only. Mijn Aansluiting identifies Liander/PWN/Ziggo responsibility, NBNL provides one planning sample and HWH provides partial assets, but none establishes physical connectivity, live load/pressure, backup, outage, repair or cross-sector restoration.
findings.action: Restrict road/rail/GTFS/NDW evidence to mobility and explicitly evidenced supply. Request safe sector-specific aggregate service zones and recovery bands; if topology is unavailable or sensitive, retain Unknown or a clearly synthetic non-spatial index without operator attribution.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure cannot represent Agriport, agriculture, port, station and other time-varying activity populations or external dependencies.
findings.evidence: Bedrijventerrein Agriport contains 640 registered residents, 100 businesses and 295 non-residential buildings, while the municipality identifies it as an above-regional agri-energy-data/greenhouse cluster. Resident counts do not capture workers, contractors, visitors, production, stock or downstream customers.
findings.action: Keep official residents unchanged, but add separate timestamped worker/visitor/activity and critical-service exposure dimensions when authoritative data is available. Until then show occupancy and downstream consequences as Unknown; never manufacture people or service load from buildings, firms, MW or land area.

findings.summary: Dispersed-settlement care, communications and rail/road access are context-only and cannot drive first-72-hour prioritisation.
findings.evidence: The public context has no RIVM acute-care point inside GM1911, one rail station, 77 transit stops, 137 antennas and 28 education sites; nearest ED references are roughly 20 km straight-line from the municipal centre. The model has no route-valid referral, vulnerable occupancy, antenna coverage/backup or emergency-support-point state.
findings.action: Add non-sensitive facility roles, referral catchments, accessibility, communications dependency and time-varying occupancy only from authorized feeds; compute event-valid travel/isolation and explicit Unknown capacity. Define owner/trigger/confirmation for welfare checks, transport assistance and emergency-support activation.

findings.summary: River, earthquake, wildfire/smoke, cyber, heat and winter results are narrow synthetic exercises, not local all-clear or forecast states.
findings.evidence: River depth/affected are exact zero at T+24/T+72 only for the canonical major-river preset; wildfire T+24 has zero flame/affected but smoke 0.211134; earthquake current motion is zero. No local ignition, earthquake, cyber target or event-valid weather is selected.
findings.action: Retain scoped direct-versus-indirect and synthetic labels. Add a local event only when source, footprint/target, effective time, units, uncertainty and NoData are explicit; never interpret a zero preset metric or empty catalogue query as safety.

findings.summary: The complete numerical, checkpoint, allocation, ledger and recovery-accounting contract passes for GM1911.
findings.evidence: The mandatory gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/deterministic, zero intensity is exact, local/service totals reconcile, ledgers close, burden is monotone and layer selection is invariant.
findings.action: Keep GM1911 and national ALL coverage in regression; add event-selection, hazard-specific ranking, water-chain, Afsluitdijk gateway, activity exposure, service-route separation and Unknown-versus-zero assertions.

corrections.summary: Replace generic GM1911 coastal screening with a named defence-aware Wadden Sea/IJsselmeer/polder event contract and honest unsupported states.
corrections.validation: Use LIWO professional layers (national scenario releases; 2025.1.6; layer-specific resolution/licence/NoData and expert interpretation required), HHNK legal/project water-defence services (regional/local, project/assessment dated; machine export/licence/cadence must be agreed) and RWS Waterinfo point observations (national point network; generally ten-minute and CC0; public/non-mission-critical) against the full 10,547-position CBS 2025 boundary. Require named event/version, Wadden/IJsselmeer boundary/tide/surge, defence segment/state, breach/overtopping, probability, unit/datum, CRS/cell, connected compartment, arrival, duration, recession/dewatering, effective time, uncertainty, coverage, NoData and licence. residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation plan, outage statement, road/rail guarantee or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood sums need not equal the municipality total; null statistics, provider, water, care, fuel, traffic or forecast results are Unknown, not zero.
The three BAG label-point mismatches are not evidence that Zijdewind, Den Oever or Wieringerwerf are outside Hollands Kroon; full BAG place polygons and aligned editions still require reconciliation.
The 245-position overview is suitable for selection/display, not defence, hydraulic, waterbody, terrain, asset, facility or route intersection; use the full 10,547-position official geometry.

LIWO candidate points, HHNK assessments/projects and municipal policy identify plausible mechanisms but not a selected breach, current failure, inundation footprint, probability, arrival, duration or dewatering curve.
Waterinfo observations are timestamped points at Den Oever, not municipal depths or future defence state; the public retrieval has no T+72 forecast and that absence is NoData.
HWH's 1,166 assigned objects do not provide validated connected catchments, units, live gate/pump state, available capacity, backup, failure or restoration; contributor completeness varies.
NWB/NDW, ProRail/GTFS, Mijn Aansluiting, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM registers do not establish live continuity, occupancy, capacity, topology, passability, backup or repair.

Registered residents do not equal people present at Agriport, agriculture/greenhouses, ports, stations, schools, care sites, workplaces, tourism or events; no authoritative event-time occupancy is consumed.

No complete public physical electricity, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, facility, fuel, stock, staffing, backup, repair or restoration topology is consumed; unavailable/security-sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
The exact-zero major-river preset is narrowly scoped and does not mean no Wadden Sea, IJsselmeer, Amstelmeer, canal, boezem, polder, groundwater, salinity, rainfall or drainage pathway.
Earthquake, remote smoke and cyber remain exercises without a selected local event/target; a catalogue origin, air station, forest name or empty spatial match is not a hazard or all-clear surface.

Recovery after T+72, cross-boundary water and utility catchments, Afsluitdijk operational coupling, acute-care referral, evacuation, mutual aid, staffing, stocks and responder/resource constraints remain outside locally validated scope.
